query: What is toxic shame, and how is it different from guilt?
why_in_two_sentences: Annie Wright's page is the strongest competitor in this batch: it opens with a side-by-side toxic-shame-versus-healthy-guilt table (exactly the query's second half), adds neurobiology, a systemic lens, references, and a visible LMFT license number. Ours is deeper on lived mechanism (why evidence never lands, why success makes it worse, the apology-settles-guilt test) with 34 FAQs, so the pages split the query: she wins the fast definitional comparison, we win everything after it. (The #2 organic result, WebMD, fetched without its article body; the next article result, Psychology Today, was judged instead.)
what_the_winner_does_that_we_dont: Opens with a side-by-side toxic shame vs healthy guilt comparison table, answering the query's second half in one glance
Includes a neurobiology-of-shame section with a references list at the end
Displays the author's LMFT license number and a clinical review date
Adds a systemic-lens section (shame as social control) that neither we nor Psychology Today cover
Addresses the driven, high-functioning reader explicitly as a named audience
what_we_do_that_they_dont: The apology test: guilt points at a repair and settles once made, shame has nothing to fix because the whole person is the subject
Explains why evidence and reassurance never land, and what the self-criticism originally protected
Explains why success intensifies shame instead of resolving it
Asks whether some shame is useful rather than treating all of it as pathology
34 verbatim FAQs including CPTSD, the four types of shame, the term's origin, and how it shows up in the body

above_the_fold.ours: H1 is the query, the short answer gives the report-versus-verdict split with the apology test, then recognition sentences; the differential is there but as prose.
above_the_fold.theirs: Annie Wright puts the full comparison table directly under the title, above any prose; the query's second half is answered in the first screen.
above_the_fold.gap: Convert the answer-box differential into a small two-column table (shame: verdict about what you are; guilt: report about what you did); the query is a comparison and a table is its natural format.

questions_they_answer_that_we_dont: My inner critic is relentless. Is that toxic shame?
I've tried affirmations and positive self-talk but they don't touch the shame. Why?
trust_signals: Annie Wright shows an LMFT license number, a clinical review date, and a references list; Psychology Today shows an editor review; ours names no one and cites nothing.
one_change_with_most_traffic_impact: Add the side-by-side shame-versus-guilt table at the top; it is the exact format the query's second half asks for and the single element that makes the competitor page faster to trust.
